user.title: Set up Device Linker
user.description: Device Linker links devices that are the same hardware, so Home Assistant shows them together under Linked devices. It looks for devices that share a MAC address or hardware identifier, or that have the same or a similar name, and links strong matches on its own. Each link shows under Device Linker, where you can edit or delete it, or add one by hand with Add link. Other matches show as discovered.

settings.title: Device Linker settings
settings.description: These settings apply to every link. Matching MAC addresses and hardware identifiers, and devices with exactly the same name, are linked automatically when automatic linking is on. With similar names on, a name that is the other name plus words like Camera or a model number (Deck Camera and G4 Deck Camera) is linked too. Other name matches show as discovered for you to confirm. A device with no area can match a device in any area; devices in two different areas never match by name.

data.match_hardware: Match MAC addresses and hardware identifiers

data_description.auto_link_similar: Links names like Deck Camera and G4 Deck Camera without asking. Names that differ by a brand or a place, like Living Room TV and Living Room Apple TV, still ask first.
data_description.auto_link_threshold: How alike two names must be to link them without asking.
data_description.suggestion_threshold: How alike two names must be to show them as discovered.
data_description.include_services: Off: services are left out, such as Daily Routine routines and Music Assistant players, which are software rather than hardware. On: they can be suggested, linked automatically and chosen in Add link like any other device.
data_description.ignored_devices: These devices are never suggested or linked automatically. Remove a device to have it suggested again. You can still link it yourself with Add link.
data_description.preferred_mac_sources: Integrations you trust to report a device's real MAC address, most trusted first, such as UniFi. When a link has a choice, the address from the first of these is picked, its device becomes the main device, and its name names the link. The order is the order you add them: to move one, remove it and add it again.

cleanup.title: Clean up leftover addresses
cleanup.description: These {count} addresses are still on a device, but no link uses them there any more, usually because the link was deleted before Device Linker kept track of which devices it changed. Each one is shown with the other devices that share it, which is why Home Assistant still shows them as linked. An address that is all a device has, or that only a service shares (such as a routine linked to its device), isn't listed. Choose the ones to remove. If you remove a MAC address the device's own integration registered, the integration adds it back on its next refresh, so a mistake does no harm.

abort.no_leftovers: No leftover addresses found. Every MAC address and shared ID Device Linker added is used by a current link.
abort.cleanup_failed: Something went wrong while cleaning up. Nothing more was changed. The details are in Settings > System > Logs, under Device Linker.
abort.cleaned: Removed {removed}. Home Assistant no longer shows those devices as linked through them.
abort.cleaned_some: Removed {removed}. Home Assistant wouldn't change {failed}, so their addresses were left as they are. The reason is in Settings > System > Logs.

rescan_suggestions.name: Rescan suggestions
rescan_suggestions.description: Look again for devices that share a MAC address or hardware identifier, or that have the same or a similar name. Strong matches are linked automatically when that setting is on.

reset_dismissed.name: Reset dismissed and unlinked
reset_dismissed.description: Forget ignored suggestions and devices you unlinked, then look again. Pairs you had separated can be linked automatically once more.

join_devices.title: Add devices to {link}
join_devices.description: Select the devices to add. They get the link's MAC address or ID, and Home Assistant shows them with the other devices in it. Devices already linked to another device, and devices from an integration already in this link, are not listed.

devices.description:
Select all devices to link to {main_name}. You can select multiple devices.

confirm.title: Confirm what the devices share
confirm.description: Selected devices: {linked_device_names}. Choose the MAC address of {main_name} to add to all selected devices. If the devices have no MAC address in common, type another ID they share instead, such as a serial number or VIN: every device, {main_name} included, gets it, and Home Assistant shows them as linked.

reconfigure.title: Edit link
reconfigure.description: Every device in this link is listed, including {main_name}, the device the MAC address came from. Each address is shown with the device it came from. Choose the address to share: the device that has it becomes the main device, and the others get it. You can also type another ID the devices share, such as a serial number or VIN. A device you remove is not linked again automatically until you run Reset dismissed and unlinked. To unlink every device, delete this link instead.
